label: Review a branch-product price difference
guardrails: A difference is a review signal, not proof that either branch has the correct price.
Do not convert this review directly into a price change without within-store price/performance evidence.
Do not claim a demand, revenue, or profit effect from branch differences alone.

label: Review a branch-product cost difference
guardrails: A cost difference authorizes investigation only; it does not establish a supplier or procurement problem.
Do not invent supplier, inventory, waste, preparation, or staffing explanations.
Do not represent a possible cost reduction as achieved or guaranteed.

label: Adjust a product price within a branch
guardrails: The target must identify both a branch and a product; company-wide and category-wide price changes are not allowed.
The change percentage must come from the store price/performance model and must not be invented by the decision model.
The action is eligible for optimization only when an action-conditioned evaluator models both price and demand response.
Branch differences may provide context but cannot independently authorize the price change.

label: Recommend a product combination as a bundle
guardrails: Only products explicitly returned together by the combination model may be bundled.
Do not invent a bundle discount, bundle price, uptake rate, duration, or profit forecast.
Historical combination frequency and gross profit do not prove incremental bundle demand or causal profitability.
The recommendation must remain owner-review-only unless a bundle-response evaluator is available.

label: Recommend products together for cross-selling
guardrails: The source and add-on products must be an explicit rule returned by the combination model.
Do not invent campaign intensity, duration, acceptance, cannibalization, or financial impact.
The recommendation must remain owner-review-only unless a cross-sell response evaluator is available.

label: Make no additional supported decision
guardrails: Use this when none of the supplied model evidence supports another allowed decision.
